definitions.explanation: Everything without exception. Has a somewhat old-fashioned or literary flavor, most commonly encountered in set phrases and compounds.

examples.japanese: {合切|がっさい}⟦{捨|す}てて→捨てる：00892_suteru⟧しまった。
examples.english: I threw away the whole lot.

examples.japanese: ⟦{荷物|にもつ}→荷物：00737_nimotsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{合切|がっさい}{袋|ぶくろ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|い}れた→入れる：01098_ireru⟧。
examples.english: I put all my belongings into a drawstring bag.

examples.japanese: ⟦{何|なに}もかも→何もかも：26777_nanimokamo⟧{合切|がっさい}⟦{引|ひ}き{受|う}ける→引き受ける：03140_hikiukeru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}って→言う：00515_iu⟧⟦くれた→くれる：00724_kureru⟧。
examples.english: They said they would take on absolutely everything.

examples.japanese: {家財|かざい}⟦{道具|どうぐ}→道具：01479_dougu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{合切|がっさい}⟦{持|も}ち{出|だ}して→持ち出す：06160_mochidasu⟧⟦{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}した→引っ越す：01171_hikkosu⟧。
examples.english: We moved out, taking every last piece of household furniture.

notes:
Composed of {合|がっ} (combine, bring together) and {切|さい} (all, entirely). The word means "everything gathered together" and has a slightly old-fashioned, literary quality. It is most commonly encountered in two forms.

The first is the standalone adverbial use meaning "everything, the whole lot," often paired with ⟦{何|なに}もかも→何もかも：26777_nanimokamo⟧ for emphasis. The second is the compound {合切|がっさい}{袋|ぶくろ}, a traditional drawstring bag used to carry all of one's personal items — the name literally means "everything bag."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {合切|がっさい}{袋|ぶくろ}: drawstring bag for carrying everything (traditional)
- ⟦{何|なに}もかも→何もかも：26777_nanimokamo⟧{合切|がっさい}: absolutely everything
- {合切|がっさい}⟦{捨|す}てる→捨てる：00892_suteru⟧: to throw away the whole lot

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{一切|いっさい}→一切：06662_issai⟧: all, everything — more common in modern usage and applies to both affirmative and negative contexts (⟦{一切|いっさい}→一切：06662_issai⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧ = none at all)
- ⟦{全部|ぜんぶ}→全部：02888_zenbu⟧: all, everything — the everyday equivalent with no literary flavor
- ⟦{丸|まる}ごと→丸ごと：10545_marugoto⟧: the whole thing, entirely — emphasizes wholeness rather than totality
